learning_outcomes.text: Understand the laws of heat transmission and perform energy balances for steady-state and transient systems.
Perform energy balances for the combustion process, applying this procedure to the sizing and operational analysis of heat generation equipment and installations, such as boilers.
Understand the concept of refrigeration and air conditioning, understanding the importance of new refrigerants on the environment.
Apply the fundamental laws of heat transmission and thermal balances to thermal engines; reciprocating internal combustion and gas engines.

syllabus_topics: Simple and multiple mechanical compression system
Fundamentals of internal combustion engines. Fundamental equations.
Fundamentals of external combustion engines. Fundamental equations.
teaching_methods: Determination of heating value of fuels
Determination of the COP of a refrigeration machine
Identification of boiler elements and their operation
Identification of biomass gasifier elements and calculation of thermal power
assessment_rules: The written exam (AE1) contributes 80% to the final grade; a minimum of 4 out of 10 points is required to pass this part, with at least 2 points from theoretical content and 2 points from problems. If less than 4 points are obtained in AE1, AE2 and AE3 will not be added, and the AE1 score will be the final grade. Laboratory practices (AE2) contribute 10%, and attendance is mandatory to pass, being non-recoverable. Monitoring tasks (AE3) contribute 10% and are non-recoverable. To pass the course, a minimum total score of 5 out of 10 (AE1+AE2+AE3) must be obtained. The written exam (AE1) is recoverable in the extraordinary call; AE2 and AE3 grades are kept for all calls of the course.
